lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Don't stand around, Junior Encoder. Remember what we discussed.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: The draft letter is missing the official Student Council tracking code.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Go find Kim in the classroom—

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Get that code from her first so we can finalize the request.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: And listen closely when you format that letter: styling matters.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Bold is loud. It tells the eye, 'Look here first!' That's why the Subject line gets Bold—so Director Reyes can't pretend he didn't see our urgent request.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Italics are quiet and classy. Use Italics for official names like 'The Paragon' and that tracking code.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: It looks professional without screaming in the reader's face.

lines.speaker: Kiko
lines.text: Bold to grab attention, italics for formal names. Got it! Let's find Kim.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Find Kim, get that tracking code, and format the letter. Bold the urgent subject, and italicize the official names. Don't make silly mistakes.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: We need this budget approved. Don't let bad formatting give them an excuse to ignore us.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Exquisite. The bold subject line gives it immediate urgency, and the designations look authoritative.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Mr. Reyes won't be able to ignore this. Excellent work, Junior Encoder.
